:::{#sol-double-complement-practice}

A vector $\vecf{w}$ is in $(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp$
exactly when $c\,(-2, 1) \cdot \vecf{w} = c\,(-2 w_1 + w_2) = 0$ for every $c$,
that is, when $w_2 = 2 w_1$.
So

$$
(\mathcal{S}^\perp)^\perp = \cb{(w_1, 2 w_1) : w_1 \in \reals} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 2)} = \mathcal{S},
$$

as @thm-double-complement says.

:::
